description: Verify that TCP allows a received RST segment to include data and transitions to CLOSED silently (RFC 1122 §4.2.2.12 p87 / RFC 793 §3.4)
approach:
[Objective]
A RST that carries payload is unusual but legal. RFC 1122 §4.2.2.12 says receivers SHOULD process it: drop the data, transition to CLOSED silently — no response packet (otherwise an attacker could induce traffic by injecting RST+data).

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester ⇄ DUT: handshake.
2. Tester → DUT: RST + data.
3. Observation: DUT must NOT respond; verify-probe afterwards elicits a RST (DUT moved to CLOSED).

[Pass condition]
No immediate DUT response to the RST+data; verify-probe gets RST.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_handshake_ack — handshake never completed
• Fail_dut_response_to_rst — DUT responded to RST+data
• Fail_no_verify_rst — DUT did not move to CLOSED (no RST to verify-probe)

verdicts.Pass: DUT silently transitioned to CLOSED on RST+data — normal
verdicts.Fail_dut_response_to_rst: DUT emitted response to RST with data in EST
verdicts.Fail_no_verify_rst: DUT did not emit RST after RST with data in EST
